missionPremise: P-211's close (_inbox/2026-09-15_p211-six-county-circle-back_close.json, member 3 caveat_undeployedFix) found that the deployed parcel-envelope-cells image accepted --county=48209 on a real production apply and silently discarded it; Hays-only scoping in that real apply was achieved entirely by the pre-existing unaccounted-only write gate, not the flag the operator believed was bounding the write. This dispatch's own framing, stated explicitly and honored here: merging PR #153 (which gives --county a working implementation on both jobs) is NOT the fix, because a flag that works today is not a flag that refuses when it is not understood -- if the image ever drifts behind the caller again, a merged-and-working flag returns to being silently discarded. The actual defect is permissive argument parsing (flagValues/hasFlag read only what they are told to look for and never notice anything else), and the fix is strict parsing: an unknown, misspelled, or unconsumed flag must cause the job to exit non-zero and write nothing, on both writer jobs, with --county's own validation as one required instance of that control.
completionPredicate: Both jobs refuse (non-zero exit, no store opened) on: (a) --county naming a FIPS that does not exist, (b) any unrecognized or misspelled flag name -- verified against the CURRENT deployed image's own source as the before-state and against this lane's fix as the after-state, on both the parse function directly and the full run function with hermetic (non-network) fakes. A valid, in-scope --county must still let the job run to completion and correctly bound its query scope, not blanket-refuse. THIS IS SATISFIED AND VERIFIED FOR THE CODE: PR #154 is open, every check-run's conclusion field reads 'success' (test, gate8, ldt-sha-comment-presence -- read via gh api, not the printed gh pr checks label), and all four pre-registered falsifiers behaved exactly as designed. IT IS NOT YET SATISFIED FOR THE DEPLOYED SURFACE: the two running Cloud Run jobs still carry the pre-fix digests named above and remain silently permissive to an unknown flag in production RIGHT NOW. Per AGENT_CONTRACT/DEV_PROCESS 4.4 ('code-done is not customer-done... a new revision is not the serving revision until verified'), that gap is real and is the reason this closes closed-partial rather than closed -- not a hedge, a fact: closing the gap requires a merge and a deploy, both explicitly reserved for the integration seat by this dispatch's own 'Do not' list.

(2) --countyy=48209 / --not-a-flag (bogus/misspelled flags): before-state ran silently (ok:true, both jobs, both bogus shapes); after-fix refuses UNKNOWN_ARGUMENT. FIRED as anticipated -- this is the exact shape the dispatch called out as identical to the original defect. (3) --county=48209 (valid, in-scope): after-fix runs to completion (ok:true), and the resolved county scope was confirmed (not merely observed) to actually reach CITY_ALL_PARCELS_SQL's own query parameters, not just the returned summary object -- a refusal that refuses everything did NOT happen. fleetMemoryScratch.text: 2026-09-15T17:2x live: factory-parcel-envelope-cells deployed digest sha256:ec2cd3bff... gen 4; factory-parcel-setback-cells deployed digest sha256:2899bbae... gen 3 (project hauska-prod-497015, region us-east4). Both confirmed via gcloud run jobs describe, cross-checked against Cloud Build history (builds 5117ed22/b5d35184, both created ~2026-09-14T22:45:2x-34Z, the same P-200 merge event #152).

A job's own flag-reading helpers (flagValue/flagValues/hasFlag in this repo's cli-flags.mjs) can be individually correct and still compose into a permissive parser: each helper only ever looks for what it is told to look for, so nothing in the existing code path ever notices an argv token none of them were asked about. A strict-parsing gate (assertKnownFlags here) has to be a SEPARATE, explicit, closed-list check called first -- it cannot be retrofitted by auditing individual flag readers one at a time, since none of them are wrong in isolation.

To establish a real before-state for a 'the deployed image silently accepts X' finding without executing a live Cloud Run job (expensive, and --apply=false dry runs still hit production Neon databases for reads): confirm the worktree's git HEAD at branch-cut time against the deployed digest via TWO independent signals (git commit identity + Cloud Build image-tag timing/digest correlation), then invoke the actual parse/run functions directly with hermetic fakes. This reproduces the deployed code's real behavior with zero network calls and zero production credentials, and is far cheaper than a live job execution for proving an argument-parsing defect specifically (the defect lives entirely before any I/O).

PR #153 and PR #154 both add equivalent --county validation to the same two functions, arrived at independently by two different lanes (P-211 and P-229) on the same day. Neither lane reconciled with the other, per each dispatch's own scope boundary. Whoever merges either PR first will very likely hit a real conflict when merging the second -- this is a live coordination gap in how OPS-24 dispatches were sequenced (P-211 dispatched 2026-09-15 morning per its own snapshot, P-229 dispatched later the same day, both touching the same lines), not something either lane could have resolved unilaterally.
